aidb_assessment.novelty: The extraction-and-consolidation method is explicitly not claimed as the main novelty. The original contribution is the deployment-centered empirical account: model-dependent memory dose, preservation of long-tail guidance, provenance invariants, recurrence-versus-correctness failure, scaffold confounding, cost accounting, and silent operational faults.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The paper deserves close reading as an engineering and evaluation guide, but not unqualified adoption of its performance claims. Test-set configuration selection, mostly single-run measurements, scaffold confounding, and absent correctness/recency control materially weaken causal and deployment-safety conclusions. AIDB should treat the pipeline as a promising reference design requiring independent repeated evaluation and a harm-aware maintenance layer.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for teams building agent memory systems. The paper supplies actionable design and evaluation practices and exposes failure modes often omitted from benchmark reports. Its quantitative conclusions are strongest for the large DeepSeek dose trend and the replicated GLM-5.3-Flash CUGA result; smaller deltas should not drive adoption decisions.

executive_summary: The paper studies self-distilled procedural memory for LLM agents: lessons are extracted from train/dev trajectories, consolidated into provenance-bearing guidelines, then injected wholesale or selected at inference. Its strongest controlled evidence is model-dependent dose response: DeepSeek-V3.2 improves monotonically to the full set, while gpt-oss-120b does better with a small retrieved subset than with all guidelines. The work is unusually valuable for documenting failures—harmful high-support advice, lost provenance, noisy single runs, scaffold confounding, and silent infrastructure faults. However, configuration selection used test_normal because no held-out validation split remained, most central results are single runs, and the system lacks automatic correctness, contradiction, staleness, or recency handling. The deployment evidence is encouraging but mixed: the clearest replicated CUGA gain comes with GLM-5.3-Flash, while GPT-4.1 deltas remain below the paper’s own noise threshold.

assumptions: Benchmark evaluator outcomes are valid labels for whether extracted evidence came from successful or failed behavior.
Train/dev trajectories are representative enough to produce guidance transferable to the test tasks.
Source-task embedding similarity is useful for retrieval, although the reported task-level analysis did not show it predicting improvement.
Using the same model for acting, extraction, and consolidation represents the intended self-improvement deployment setting.
Task and scenario completion changes can be interpreted only relative to run-to-run noise and a fixed agent scaffold.
key_components: Trajectory capture through instrumented clients, observability-store synchronization, or an MCP submission tool.
Outcome-grounded lesson extraction from both successes and failures; success polarity comes from the evaluator rather than model self-report.
Support-conserving consolidation that clusters near-duplicates, merges equivalent advice, and carries uncovered lessons through unchanged.
Static full-memory injection or dose-controlled retrieval using support, source-task similarity, and deduplication.
Pluggable storage and MCP delivery through tools including get_guidelines, get_relevant_guidelines, and save_trajectory.
Operational checks added after failures: conservation regression tests, per-task exception handling, minimum model-call assertions, progress watchdogs, and store-growth checks.
method.overview: The agent is run on benchmark train and dev tasks, retaining successful and failed trajectories. The same model used by the agent extracts one to three imperative lessons per trajectory. Lessons are embedded, clustered by source-task embeddings, and merged only within clusters; uncovered lessons pass through unchanged. Consolidation conserves total support and retains evidence polarity and provenance. At inference, the system either injects all guidelines or combines an always-present high-support core with task-similar retrieved guidelines, deduplicating candidates. No separate teacher model or human labeling is used.

open_questions: Can a held-out validation protocol choose memory dose reliably without consuming the benchmark test split?
Which observable model properties predict whether full, support-thresholded, or retrieval-based delivery will be optimal?
How should guideline correctness, contradiction, recency, and task-level harm be represented and updated over time?
Can rare support-one guidelines be selected using calibrated utility estimates rather than embedding similarity alone?
Do the reported gains persist across repeated runs, new task distributions, changing APIs, and longer-lived production memory stores?
How much of the gain comes from extracting from successful trajectories versus failure trajectories?
Can static-prefix caching preserve full-memory accuracy while materially reducing billed input cost and latency?

problem.importance: Recurring mistakes such as incorrect pagination, wrong entity resolution, duplicate side-effecting calls, and answering when no answer was requested can reduce reliability in deployed agents. A memory mechanism must therefore improve completion without overwhelming weaker models, corrupting provenance, or silently introducing harmful rules.
problem.scope: The study covers an offline extraction–consolidation–delivery pipeline, primarily measured with the AppWorld reference ReAct agent and six memory-enabled models. It also reports CUGA evaluations on AppWorld and the retail split of τ-bench, plus one qualitative watsonx Orchestrate transfer trace. It does not establish performance for arbitrary agent architectures, continually updated unattended memory, or production populations at scale.
problem.statement: Long-horizon LLM agents repeatedly make procedural rather than factual errors. The paper asks whether an agent can improve by distilling its own trajectories into reusable guidance, and how much such memory should be delivered to models of different capability.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Compare no memory, inject all, fixed support cores, and retrieval under the paper’s current test-selected protocol versus selection on a newly held-out validation partition.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A validation-selected dose policy will retain the advantage of retrieval for weaker models and full lossless memory for stronger models on a genuinely untouched test set.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Test-set TGC lift over no memory, accompanied by SGC, tokens per task, and the mean with a confidence interval across at least five matched runs.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop when every model–dose arm has at least five completed matched runs and the confidence interval for the selected policy’s TGC difference versus inject-all is narrow enough to exclude a five-task-equivalent noise band, or when a prespecified compute budget is exhausted.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Support-only consolidation and retrieval exactly as described in the paper, compared with the same store augmented by per-guideline harm, contradiction, and recency signals.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Adding outcome-based down-voting and recency/contradiction handling will reduce guideline-induced regressions without erasing the completion gain of lossless memory.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Number of baseline-passed tasks regressed by memory, with overall TGC and SGC as co-reported guardrails.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after a prespecified stream of repeated and shifted tasks when the augmented system either reduces regressions without a statistically credible TGC loss, or fails to reduce regressions across two consecutive evaluation checkpoints.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The reported retrieval scheme using a high-support core plus source-task embedding similarity and deduplication.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Guideline-level utility learned from counterfactual task replays will outperform source-task cosine similarity for selecting rare, support-one guidance at equal token cost.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: TGC at a matched per-task input-token budget, with calibration between predicted guideline utility and observed task outcome change.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after each candidate selector has been evaluated on the same held-out tasks across at least five matched runs and either the utility selector exceeds the baseline outside the measured noise band or its confidence interval rules out a practically meaningful gain.

artifacts: The paper states that the pipeline is available in the open-source altk-evolve library.
It names concrete configuration controls: consolidation_mode, min_support, core_support, retrieval_top_k, and injection_mode.
It specifies benchmark splits, principal model/scaffold combinations, guideline counts, completion metrics, token costs, and selected repeated-run ranges.
The references identify support-conserving consolidation and dosage-aware retrieval changes in named pull requests.
reproducibility.assessment: The described open-source implementation and detailed operational narrative make the pipeline inspectable in principle, but the supplied paper evidence is insufficient for exact numerical reproduction. Reproduction would require reconstructing prompts and configurations and obtaining or regenerating trajectory-level artifacts. The single-run primary results and test-set configuration search further limit confirmatory reproducibility.
missing: Exact extraction, consolidation, and inference prompts are not supplied in the document blocks.
Model endpoint versions, decoding settings beyond the temperature-zero discussion, seeds, and full runtime environment are not comprehensively specified.
The exact per-model configurations behind every reported point are not fully enumerated.
Raw trajectories, extracted lessons, consolidated guideline sets, task-level outcomes, and evaluation logs are not stated to be released.
No held-out configuration-selection split is available for the primary AppWorld study.
Most central results lack repeated-run distributions, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

results.context: This is the paper’s strongest dose-response result for the reference ReAct scaffold, although individual adjacent dose changes were within noise and the configurations were evaluated directly on test_normal.

evidence.quote: DeepSeek-V3.2 climbs 79.8 → 82.7 → 83.9 → 85.7 → 89.3 TGC as the injected set grows from 0 to 12 to 19 to 47 to all 191 guidelines.
SGC rises from 64.3 to 80.4.
The gain holds on the hard split (60.4 → 72.9 TGC, 41.7 → 58.3 SGC).

results.result: On AppWorld test_normal, DeepSeek-V3.2 rose from 79.8 TGC without memory to 89.3 TGC with all 191 guidelines; SGC rose from 64.3 to 80.4. The hard-split improvement was also substantial, from 60.4 to 72.9 TGC and from 41.7 to 58.3 SGC.

results.context: The selected configuration was chosen among configurations run on test_normal, so its advantage over the fixed all-guidelines rule is exploratory rather than clean held-out model selection.

evidence.quote: gpt-oss-120b starts at 39.9. With all 199 guidelines it scores 51.2.
Its best result comes from about 29 selected guidelines: 55.4 TGC, the mean of two runs (56.0 and 54.8).
That is seven tasks above the full set, at essentially baseline token cost (116K vs. 110K per task).

results.result: For gpt-oss-120b, full injection raised TGC from 39.9 to 51.2, but retrieval of about 29 guidelines achieved mean TGC 55.4 across two runs, with 116K tokens per task versus 110K at baseline. This shows a non-monotonic dose response for the weakest tested model.

results.context: This ablation supports retaining rare situational lessons for capable models, but does not isolate which support-one guidelines caused the gain.

results.result: Compression was materially worse for DeepSeek-V3.2: 12 compressed guidelines produced +2.9 TGC, whereas 191 losslessly consolidated guidelines produced +9.5 TGC; 144 of the full guidelines had support one.

results.context: This is a consequential negative result demonstrating that frequency-based support can amplify incorrect advice. The fix was manual, and the pipeline still lacks an automatic harm or contradiction signal.

results.result: In the repaired CUGA integration with GLM-5.3-Flash, the full 164-guideline set increased mean TGC from 87.8 to 93.2 and SGC from 84.8 to 88.4 over two runs per arm, while tokens per task increased by 36%. A 29-guideline subset remained within noise of baseline.

title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents

uncertainties.uncertainty: It is unclear whether memory dose is best predicted by baseline capability itself or by correlated factors such as context handling, instruction following, extraction quality, or consolidation quality.
uncertainties.why_it_matters: A deployment policy needs a measurable selector for dose; model identity and baseline score alone may not transfer across tasks or scaffolds.
